Posterior predictive checks

Source: R/ppc.R
psp_ppc.Rd

Simulates replicated outcomes from the posterior and compares summary statistics of the replicates with those of the observed outcomes (Gelman, Meng and Stern 1996). Replicates are drawn for the same units, periods and regressors, conditional on the posterior draws of the random effects kept by the sampler (pooled models have none). Missing outcomes are left out of every statistic.

Usage

psp_ppc(fit, draws = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A fitted psprobit object.

draws

Number of posterior draws to replicate (default control$impacts_draws).

seed

Optional seed for the replicates.

Value

An object of class psp_ppc: a list with, for each statistic, the observed values (observed), the replicated values (replicated, draws x components) and posterior predictive p-values \(P(T(y^{rep}) \ge T(y))\) (ppp). Its print() method shows a summary.

Details

The statistics are:

  • share: the share of each outcome category (of \(y = 1\) for binary models) in each period;

  • moran: Moran's I of the outcome (category codes for ordered models) in each period, which checks the spatial dependence;

  • persistence: the share of units whose outcome equals that of the previous period, which checks the dependence over time (\(T \ge 2\)).

References

Gelman, A., Meng, X.-L. and Stern, H. (1996). Posterior predictive assessment of model fitness via realized discrepancies. Statistica Sinica 6, 733-807.

Examples

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(5, 5), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 4, beta = c(0, 1, -1), rho = 0.5, seed = 1)
fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1 + x2, d, c("id", "time"), W, impacts = FALSE,
                control = psp_control(iter = 300, warmup = 200, chains = 1, seed = 1))
#> Warning: Possible convergence problems (R-hat > 1.01 or bulk ESS < 100) for: (Intercept), x1, x2, rho, sigma_alpha. Consider more iterations.
psp_ppc(fit, draws = 50, seed = 1)
#> Posterior predictive checks (50 replicates)
#> ppp = P(T(y_rep) >= T(y)); values near 0 or 1 signal misfit.
#> 
#> share:
#>            observed rep_mean rep_q2.5 rep_q97.5  ppp
#> P(y=1) t=1     0.48    0.552    0.320     0.680 0.84
#> P(y=1) t=2     0.64    0.630    0.449     0.791 0.60
#> P(y=1) t=3     0.52    0.502    0.360     0.680 0.50
#> P(y=1) t=4     0.60    0.529    0.258     0.680 0.34
#> 
#> moran:
#>           observed rep_mean rep_q2.5 rep_q97.5  ppp
#> Moran t=1    0.145    0.084   -0.213     0.332 0.32
#> Moran t=2    0.282    0.149   -0.090     0.394 0.18
#> Moran t=3   -0.100   -0.009   -0.290     0.276 0.70
#> Moran t=4    0.283    0.103   -0.146     0.386 0.08
#> 
#> persistence:
#>             observed rep_mean rep_q2.5 rep_q97.5  ppp
#> persist t=2     0.68    0.568    0.400     0.782 0.26
#> persist t=3     0.64    0.621    0.480     0.760 0.50
#> persist t=4     0.60    0.609    0.449     0.760 0.66
